paper.title: Mechanically adaptive hydrogels reprogram apoptotic cell clearance to prevent tissue fibrosis

core_intervention.name: Gel/VP mechanically adaptive hydrogel
core_intervention.components: AAm/CSMA interpenetrating network with CNC@PDA@ZIF8 nanonodes and verteporfin
core_intervention.intended_action: reverse mechanical buffering plus sustained YAP-pathway modulation
core_intervention.clock_implication: does not identify a late safe-EXIT onset because treatment begins before the repair state is established

evidence_modules.details: Yoda1 stimulation for 24 h increased Ca2+/ROS, Piezo1/YAP1 signaling and cell death; apoptotic HUVECs were then used as a defined downstream perturbation.

evidence_modules.module: apoptotic endothelial cells -> fibroblast scar phenotype
evidence_modules.details: Yoda1-induced apoptotic endothelial cells were collected and co-cultured with fibroblasts for 24 h; COL-1, COL-3 and alpha-SMA increased.
Macrophages were exposed to material for 24 h, then Yoda1 for 24 h, then apoptotic endothelial cells for 4 h. Gel/VP restored phagocytic activity strongly under the perturbed condition.

evidence_modules.module: restored macrophage state -> reduced fibroblast activation
evidence_modules.details: Conditioned medium from macrophages receiving apoptotic-cell uptake plus Gel/VP intervention reduced fibrosis-associated markers including alpha-SMA in BLM-activated fibroblasts.

Immediate wound application in a rat 16-mm full-thickness skin-defect model was associated with reduced YAP activation, reparative macrophage shift, fewer alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts, more ordered collagen remodeling and less scar formation at the reported wound-healing endpoints.

mechanistic_chain_audit.reason: the full Piezo1/YAP -> apoptotic-cell retention -> efferocytosis -> alpha-SMA sequence is assembled from linked perturbation modules plus sparse in-vivo endpoints rather than a single dense longitudinal in-vivo series

delayed_intervention_test.meaning: no arm starting after closure, after myofibroblast peak, or after structural stabilization was identified

material_mechanics.test: Instron tensile testing of 20 x 10 x 2 mm hydrogel samples at 2 mm/min, at least 3 parallel samples per group

mechanical_measurement_audit.interpretation: mechanical characterization of the material is quantitative, but there is no identified longitudinal point-level measurement of wound-tissue stiffness, local stress, or force redistribution over healing time

public_corollary_disclosure.role: corroborating experimental disclosure for timing, mechanical testing and linked mechanistic modules; not treated as peer-reviewed source data or as a substitute for article supplementary files

macrophage_phagocytic_rate.note: reported article-level headline value; patent disclosure provides mean +/- SD for the corresponding assays and additional paired values

gate_verdict.reason: mechanical intervention changes mechanotransduction, macrophage apoptotic-cell clearance and downstream fibrotic outcome, but treatment is preventive/immediate rather than delayed and no biological wound-state decay constant or safe late-EXIT boundary is identified

frozen_boundaries: mechanical buffering plus verteporfin is a compound intervention and should not be reduced to pure mechanics without component-specific evidence
linked causal modules do not equal a dense in-vivo temporal trajectory
reduced alpha-SMA accumulation is not equivalent to direct myofibroblast EXIT
immediate treatment cannot establish the timing of a safe delayed resolution intervention
material modulus is not wound-tissue stiffness
patent disclosure is not peer-reviewed source data

next_killer_test.primary: delayed-start Gel or mechanically matched drug-free buffering arms initiated after wound closure / after the alpha-SMA rise, with dense YAP, apoptotic-cell burden, macrophage efferocytosis and alpha-SMA measurements
next_killer_test.secondary: obtain article supplementary/source-data files or author-provided point-level data for Figures 2, 3, 6 and 7, including raw stress-strain traces and exact D7/D14 marker quantification
next_killer_test.clock_question: does restoring mechanical buffering after the reparative state is established accelerate resolution without impairing closure or matrix stabilization?
